definitions.explanation: A sustained human activity or way of living. Often refers to the fundamental activities that make up daily life, work, or cultural practice, with a nuance of continuity and purpose.

examples.japanese: {日々|ひび}の{営|いとな}みを{大切|たいせつ}にする。
examples.english: Value the activities of daily life.

examples.japanese: {農業|のうぎょう}は{人間|にんげん}の{最|もっと}も{古|ふる}い{営|いとな}みのひとつだ。
examples.english: Agriculture is one of humanity's oldest pursuits.

examples.japanese: この{地域|ちいき}では{何百年|なんびゃくねん}も{前|まえ}から{漁|りょう}の{営|いとな}みが{続|つづ}いている。
examples.english: In this region, the practice of fishing has continued for hundreds of years.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {人間|にんげん}の{営|いとな}み (human activity/endeavor)
- {日々|ひび}の{営|いとな}み (daily pursuits)
- {生活|せいかつ}の{営|いとな}み (the activities of daily life)
- {営|いとな}みを{続|つづ}ける (continue a livelihood/practice)

The nominalized form of the verb {営|いとな}む (to conduct, to carry on). Has a literary and somewhat elevated register, often used in essays, documentaries, and reflective writing to describe fundamental human activities with a sense of dignity and continuity.
